title: Kinds of Memory
brief: Priya uses your meal-planning assistant three times this month. In session 1 she says she is vegetarian, allergic to peanuts and cooks for two. In sessions 2 and 3 she just asks for a plan. Right now the agent only has working memory (the context window), so every session starts from zero. Get at least 85% of sessions right in 1.5 turns or fewer on average.

tasks.label: Session 1: first visit
tasks.prompt: I'm vegetarian, allergic to peanuts, and I cook for two. What should we have for dinner tonight?

tasks.label: Session 2: a week later
tasks.prompt: Plan five dinners for this week, please.

tasks.label: Session 3: two weeks later
tasks.prompt: Quick snack idea for a long train ride tomorrow?

ask.text: Before I plan anything: do you have any dietary restrictions or allergies, and how many people are eating? (Priya, typing it all again: "Vegetarian, peanut allergy, two of us. I told you this last time.")

search_episodes.text: memory.search("Priya diet") → 3 old transcript snippets: "...dinner for two...", "...my sister eats fish...", "...peanut sauce recipe for a party..."

generic.text: Here's your week: Monday chicken stir-fry, Tuesday satay noodles with peanut sauce, Wednesday salmon, Thursday beef chili, Friday pizza for four.

personal.text: Vegetarian, peanut-free, for two: Monday chickpea curry, Tuesday mushroom risotto, Wednesday black bean tacos, Thursday halloumi traybake, Friday veggie pizza.

modifiers.note: The preferences are right there in the prompt.
After asking again, the model has what it needs, one turn late.
Semantic memory: the saved profile (vegetarian, peanut allergy, cooks for two) is in the prompt from turn 1.
Episodic memory: the model searches old transcripts first.
Old snippets are noisy: the sister's fish and the party's peanut sauce leak into the plan.

goals.label: Get at least 85% of sessions right
1.5 turns or fewer on average (no asking again)

hints: Read session 2 in the transcript. Where would the agent have to look to know Priya is vegetarian?
The Memory node's kind is 'window': that is working memory, and it is gone when the session ends. Which kind keeps facts about the user between sessions?
Set the Memory node's kind to 'profile' (semantic memory: stable facts about the user) and keep the write policy on.
explain: Working memory dies with the session. A small profile of stable facts, loaded into every prompt, is the right kind of memory for preferences; searching old transcripts (episodic memory) is slower and drags in noise.
